newsitem.title: USA: Transcrypt to restructure E.F. Johnson.
newsitem.headline: Transcrypt to restructure E.F. Johnson.

text.p: Transcrypt International Inc said Wednesday it will restructure its newly acquired E.F. Johnson Co subsidiary, which has recently incurred operating losses and cash flow difficulties.
E.F. Johnson develops and makes wireless communications products and systems for the land mobile radio (LMR) market.

Unde a restructuring program which will be implemented immediately, 25 percent of E.F. Johnson's 550 employees will lose their jobs; low margin products and services will be phase-out; and the company's corporate headquarters will be consolidated.

"Transcrypt is focused on restructuring EFJ for current and future levels of business, and we are confident that our plan will yield immediate results," said Jeff Fuller, Transcrypt president and chief executive officer.

Transcrypt said about 25 percent of the 550 EFJ employees in Burnsville and Waseca, Minn. have received notices that their jobs are being eliminated effective today. The terminations included severance packages.

"Transcrypt has invested $6 million into EFJ to fund severance programs, cancellation payments for duplicative expenses and to reduce accounts payable. These programs will allow EFJ to resume shipping on a timely schedule and reduce operating losses," said Scott Bocklund, senior vice president of finance, said in a news release.

E.F. Johnson's corporate offices will be consolidated at Transcrypt's Lincoln, Neb. headquarters. The company will continue to have a sales office in Minnesota along with a product manufacturing and engineering facility in Waseca.
Transcrypt provides information security and wireless communication products. E.F. Johnson is the third largest manufacturer of land mobile radios in the U.S.
